    AI Overview
    The 152nd Kentucky Derby is scheduled for Saturday, May 2, 2026, at Churchill Downs in Louisville, KY, with post time expected around 6:57 p.m. ET. As the first leg of the Triple Crown, this premier event concludes a full week of racing celebrations beginning April 25, 2026. Tickets, including premium packages, are available through Official Derby Experiences. 
    Key 2026 Contenders & Prep Race Highlights 
    • So Happy: Earned a spot by winning the Santa Anita Derby, trainer Mark Glatt confirmed.
    • Fulleffort: Won the $777,000 Jeff Ruby Steaks at Turfway Park.
    • Danon Bourbon: Undefeated Japanese contender who won the Fukuryu Stakes.
    • International Challengers: Wonder Dean and Six Speed, top finishers from the UAE Derby, are expected to compete.
    • Top Contenders: Other early ranked contenders for the 2026 race include Further Ado and Renegade. 
    Key Info for 2026 Derby 
    • Event: 152nd Kentucky Derby (Grade I)
    • Date: Saturday, May 2, 2026
    • Location: Churchill Downs, Louisville, KY
    • Qualification: 20 horses earn spots via a tiered points system in designated Road to the Kentucky Derby races. 
    You can track the official 2026 leaderboard, find travel packages, and view the full racing schedule on the official Kentucky Derby website.

      As of early April 2026, Renegade is established as the favorite for the 2026 Kentucky Derby at approximately 4-1 to 12-1 odds following his Arkansas Derby win, while Commandment and Further Ado are top contenders. Other notable contenders in the futures market include The Puma (12-1), Chief Wallabee (13-1), and Paladin (8-1). 
      Here are the key contenders and early odds for the 2026 Kentucky Derby (May 2, 2026): 
      • Renegade: 4-1 to 13-1 (leads futures)
      • Commandment: 7-1 to 12-1
      • Paladin: 5-1 to 8-1
      • Further Ado: 8-1 to 10-1
      • The Puma: 12-1
      • Chief Wallabee: 8-1 to 13-1
      • Nearly: 8-1 to 12-1
      • Emerging Market: 15-1
      Note: The Kentucky Derby uses a pari-mutuel system, meaning odds fluctuate up until post time. These odds are based on early 2026 future wagers.

        AI Overview
        The 2026 Kentucky Derby, scheduled for May 2 at Churchill Downs, continues its historic traditions, including the "Run for the Roses" garland, sipping Mint Juleps, wearing elaborate hats, and singing "My Old Kentucky Home". Derby Week includes the "Dawn at the Downs" morning workouts and the Oaks Day "Pink Out" for charity. 
        Key Traditions of the Kentucky Derby 2026:
        • The Garland of Roses: The winner is draped with a blanket of over 400 red roses, a tradition that gives the race its nickname, "Run for the Roses". 
        • Mint Juleps: The official drink, made with bourbon, simple syrup, mint, and crushed ice, with over 10,000 bottles of bourbon used, honoring Kentucky's heritage. 
        • Derby Hats: A fashion staple for women and men, featuring extravagant, large-brimmed hats. 
        • "My Old Kentucky Home": Played by the University of Louisville Marching Band as the horses walk onto the track. 
        • Kentucky Oaks: Held on Friday before the Derby, focusing on fillies (3-year-old female horses) and raising cancer awareness with the color pink. 
        • The Twin Spires: The iconic architectural feature of Churchill Downs. 
        • Celebrity Attendees: High-profile guests are common at the event. 
        • Menu Favorites: Classic foods include Benedictine spread, pimento cheese, and Hot Browns. 
        Synonyms and Related Terms: 
        • Run for the Roses
        • The Most Exciting Two Minutes in Sports
        • The Fastest Two Minutes in Sports
        • Derby Week
        • Oaks Day (Friday)
        • The 152nd Running (for 2026)
        Usage Examples for 2026:
        • At the Track:
          Attendees will watch morning workouts during "Dawn at the Downs" on April 27, 2026. 
        • At Home:
          Parties will feature official cocktails, including the Oak Lily or Mint Julep. 
        • Attire:
          Guests are encouraged to wear upscale, vibrant outfits (Derby best) and, specifically on Oaks Day, wear pink to support cancer advocacy.

          AI Overview
          The 2025–2026 Road to the Kentucky Derby features a series of 36+ qualifying, or "prep," races awarding points to the top five finishers. Major March/April 2026 races include the Louisiana Derby, Florida Derby, Arkansas Derby, Wood Memorial, Blue Grass Stakes, and Santa Anita Derby. These determine the 20-horse field for the May 2, 2026, race. 
          Key Qualifying Races (Road to the Kentucky Derby 2026):
          • Championship Series (100-50-25-15-10 points):
            • Louisiana Derby: (Mar 21, 2026 - Fair Grounds) 
            • Florida Derby: (Mar 28, 2026 - Gulfstream Park) 
            • Arkansas Derby: (Mar 28, 2026 - Oaklawn Park) 
            • UAE Derby: (Mar 28, 2026 - Meydan) 
            • Wood Memorial: (Apr 4, 2026 - Aqueduct) 
            • Blue Grass Stakes: (Apr 4, 2026 - Keeneland) 
            • Santa Anita Derby: (Apr 4, 2026 - Santa Anita) 
          • Key Prep Season Races (50-25-15-10-5 points): 
            • Risen Star Stakes: (Feb 14, 2026 - Fair Grounds) 
            • Rebel Stakes: (Mar 1, 2026 - Oaklawn) 
            • Gotham Stakes: (Feb 28, 2026 - Aqueduct) 
            • San Felipe Stakes: (Mar 7, 2026 - Santa Anita) 
            • Sunland Derby: (Feb 15, 2026 - Sunland Park) 
          • Other Qualifying Races:
            • Lexington Stakes: (Apr 11, 2026 - Keeneland) 
            • Japan Road to the Kentucky Derby: (4 races) 
            • European/Middle East Road: (10 races, including UAE 2000 Guineas & Saudi Derby) 
          Synonyms/Related Terms: Kentucky Derby Prep Races, Derby Trail, Road to the Kentucky Derby, and Championship Series Races. 
          The top 17 earners on the North American road, plus invited top contenders from the Japan and Euro/MidEast paths, make up the final 20-horse field.

            AI Overview
            Tickets for the 2026 Kentucky Derby (May 1–2) range from approximately $100–$200 for general infield admission to over $1,000+ for reserved seating/hospitality per day. Two-day ticket packages often include food/drinks and generally start higher, with premium packages reaching six figures. 
            Here is a breakdown of 2026 ticket options and estimated costs based on early 2026 data:
            • General Admission (Infield): ~\$100–\$200 (access to the infield, no grandstand seat). 
            • Infield Final Turn GA: Starting at \$376.50. 
            • Frontside Plaza Walkaround: Starting at \$731.85. 
            • Reserved Seating (2-Day Packages): Starting around \$779, with, for example, 1st Floor Clubhouse seats starting at \$917.25 and 3rd Floor Covered Grandstand seats costing over \$5,000 when paired with hotel packages. 
            • Premium/VIP Packages: Options like Turf Club, Jockey Club Suites, or Premium 2-day packages range from over \$10,000 to over \$100,000. 
            Key Considerations:
            • Tickets Are Selling: Tickets are already available for the 152nd Kentucky Derby in 2026. 
            • 2-Day Requirement: Many of the best reserved seats are sold as two-day packages (Oaks and Derby). 
            • Prices Increase: The average cost of tickets has increased significantly, with 2024 ticket prices showing a 231% increase over 2014 levels, and this trend has continued. 
            Disclaimer: Prices can change, and availability is based on when tickets are purchased.
